items.title: The US Navy Retired A 10,000-Lb Cargo Workhorse For A Tiltrotor That Carries 4,000 Lbs Fewer
items.summary: On the surface level, it seems like the US Navy committed a strategic folly when it decided to replace the venerable Grumman C-2A Greyhound carrier-onboard delivery plane with a Bell Boeing tiltrotor. The newer and totally different rotary-wing aircraft has 40% less total payload than the 1960s vintage fixed-wing tail-hook plane it succeeded.
items.t: The US Navy Retired A 10,000-Lb Cargo Workhorse For A Tiltrotor That Carries 4,000 Lbs Fewer

items.title: White House Urges Congress To Approve $30 Billion In Upgrades To US Aviation Infrastructure
items.summary: The White House is urging Congress to approve an additional $30.1 billion for US aviation infrastructure upgrades. Reuters reports that Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and budget director Russell Vought are pushing for action before Democrats take control of Congress in January. The request follows the Republicans' defeat in November's midterm elections, leaving the administration with a narrowing window to secure funding.
items.t: White House Urges Congress To Approve $30 Billion In Upgrades To US Aviation Infrastructure

items.title: Airbus' Clever Engineering Tricks That Made The A330 Become The "Butter Machine"
items.summary: The Airbus A330 has earned an unusual nickname among aviation enthusiasts: the “Butter Machine.” The name comes from its reputation for exceptionally smooth landings, often marked by a gentle first contact between the rear wheels and the runway before the rest of the landing gear settles.
items.t: Airbus' Clever Engineering Tricks That Made The A330 Become The "Butter Machine"

items.title: Why New Boeing Planes Are Green Before Delivery, But Airbus Aircraft Aren't
items.summary: The observation that pre-delivery Boeing aircraft are green, and Airbus aluminum aircraft aren't, is partially true, but it is far from the full picture. There are significant differences in the substances that Boeing and Airbus' various divisions and subcontractors use , and this is partially driven by environmental regulations differing by location. But unfinished Boeing aircraft are also typically photographed at an earlier stage of development compared with Airbus.
items.t: Why New Boeing Planes Are Green Before Delivery, But Airbus Aircraft Aren't

items.title: Alaska Airlines Plans To Connect Tokyo From Anchorage, But Can Only Do It With 1 Boeing 737
items.summary: Alaska Airlines will launch its first nonstop service between Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport (ANC) and Tokyo Narita Airport (NRT) in 2027, opening a direct link between the largest city in Alaska and one of Asia’s most important aviation gateways. The route will be unusual not only because the cities have never had scheduled nonstop service on Alaska, but because the airline plans to operate it with a single-aisle aircraft. A Boeing 737 MAX 8 will cover the transpacific journey, which is scheduled to take as long as eight hours and 15 minutes westbound.
items.t: Alaska Airlines Plans To Connect Tokyo From Anchorage, But Can Only Do It With 1 Boeing 737

items.title: Is It True That The Airbus A321XLR Flies With Its Nose Pitched Up At Cruising Altitude?
items.summary: Did you feel like your plane was a little nose-up on your last long flight? Well, you're not wrong. In fact, nearly every single commercial jetliner cruises with a noticeable nose-high pitch for most of the journey. The physics of flight dictate that an aircraft on a steady level cruise rarely maintains a perfectly parallel relationship with the horizon. It's especially remarkable on Airbus ' newest long-haul narrowbody, the A321XLR.
items.t: Is It True That The Airbus A321XLR Flies With Its Nose Pitched Up At Cruising Altitude?

items.title: BREAKING: FAA halts all US departures, warns airborne flights to expect holding nationwide
items.summary:
The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop shortly before 4 p.m. Eastern time on November 13, 2026, after a communications outage affected every US Air Route Traffic Control Center (ARTCC) in the country. It was the first time since January 2023 that the agency had halted departures nationwide, and only the second nationwide ground stop since the 9/11 terror attacks in 2001.

The FAA subsequently advised crews to expect airborne holding at airports nationwide because of equipment outages. Flightradar24 reported that about 3,100 aircraft were airborne and bound for US airports during the ground stop. The tracking figure includes all US-bound flights in the air at the time. The number actually holding was unclear.

US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy described the problem as “a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers” and said FAA technicians were investigating. The regional centers direct aircraft primarily during the en route portion of a flight. Duffy’s initial statement did not identify which system had failed or give a time for departures to resume.

The nationwide order followed an earlier halt in Chicago, where air traffic controllers had encountered communications problems. Houston’s George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH) subsequently confirmed it was holding all departures. At San Francisco International Airport (SFO), spokesman Doug Yakel said aircraft already en route continued to land while departures were held.

The previous nationwide ground stop, on January 11, 2023, lasted roughly 90…
items.t: BREAKING: FAA halts all US departures, warns airborne flights to expect holding nationwide

items.title: US airlines brace for busiest travel day since pandemic amid Thanksgiving rush
items.summary:
US airlines expect to carry nearly 29 million passengers over the 2026 Thanksgiving travel weekend, with the biggest crowds due as travelers head home from family celebrations.

American Airlines has scheduled 7,021 flights for November 29, its busiest day since the pandemic, while United said it expects about 600,000 passengers that day.

Airlines for America expects November 29 and 30 to be the two busiest days of the 11-day period that begins November 20. US carriers are offering an average of 38,000 more seats per day than they did over Thanksgiving last year, according to the trade group.

The Sunday after Thanksgiving in 2025 was the busiest day the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) had ever recorded. TSA screened more than 3.13 million people at US airports on November 30, more than twice the 1.56 million who passed through checkpoints on Thanksgiving Day. Nearly 2.9 million more passed through security on December 1.

Los Angeles International (LAX) handled the most checkpoint traffic during the seven days around Thanksgiving last year. About 689,000 people went through security at LAX, followed by 647,000 at New York’s John F. Kennedy International (JFK), 603,000 at Atlanta (ATL) and 598,000 at Chicago O’Hare (ORD), according to TSA figures.

American and its regional partners expect more than 8 million passengers across nearly 85,000 flights between November 19 and December 1. The schedule includes 4% more flights than last Thanksgiving.

At midday on November 29, American said it expects to have 1,130 flights in the air at once.

United expects to…
items.t: US airlines brace for busiest travel day since pandemic amid Thanksgiving rush

items.title: How Many Crew Members Does It Take To Fly A KC-135 Stratotanker?
items.summary: First flown in 1956, the Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker has spent decades refueling US military aircraft in flight. Despite its age, it remains a major part of the United States Air Force 's tanker fleet, supporting fighters, bombers, and other aircraft on missions around the world. But how many people does it actually take to operate an aircraft responsible for such an important job? The answer raises some interesting questions about how the Stratotanker was designed and how its crew responsibilities have changed over the years.
items.t: How Many Crew Members Does It Take To Fly A KC-135 Stratotanker?

items.title: Quantum Systems says Bundeswehr drones flying again after cyberattack
items.summary:
On November 13, 2026, Quantum Systems announced that its drones operated by the Bundeswehr are flying again, after the German armed forces grounded them as a precaution following a cyberattack on the manufacturer.

“The fleet is operating normally around the globe, including Germany and the Bundeswehr,” a company spokesperson told Reuters in an emailed statement. “The Bundeswehr was the only customer to ground their systems as a precaution.”

Quantum Systems did not specify when the grounding began or ended, or how many drones were affected. The German military has not independently confirmed that flights have resumed. According to the Financial Times , the grounding prevented Quantum Systems from participating in a recent military exercise.

Cyberattack reportedly targeted Quantum Systems software updates 

In a statement published on November 12, 2026, Quantum Systems said that it had identified a cybersecurity incident at the end of October. An immediate internal investigation revealed “an active cyberattack by hostile actors,” the company claimed.

According to the German magazine Der Spiegel, the attackers placed a malicious file on a server used to distribute updates for QBase, Quantum Systems’ ground-control and mission-planning software. The company did not disclose these technical details in its public statement and nor did it identify the attackers.

Quantum Systems stressed that its IT and security teams contained the threat in cooperation with the authorities. It reported the incident to the relevant agencies, and an investigation remains underway with state…
items.t: Quantum Systems says Bundeswehr drones flying again after cyberattack

items.title: Saudi THC firms up 12-jet Bombardier order, with options for 48 more
items.summary:
Saudi Arabia’s The Helicopter Company (THC) has signed firm purchase agreements for 12 Bombardier business jets, turning a letter of intent announced at the Farnborough International Airshow in July 2026 into a binding order.

The deal, announced on November 13, 2026, covers five Challenger 3500s, five Global 5500s and two Global 8000s. Bombardier valued the order at approximately $568 million based on 2026 list prices.

The agreements also include options for another 48 aircraft across the three models, potentially bringing THC’s business jet fleet to 60 aircraft. Bombardier said THC has sole discretion over whether to exercise those options.

The manufacturer described the transaction as the largest business aviation fleet order to date in Saudi Arabia.

Saudi helicopter operator expands into business aviation 

THC is owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) and has been operating since mid-2019. Its fleet includes more than 60 helicopters used for emergency medical services, aerial work, private charter and tourism.

The Bombardier jets will be THC’s first fixed-wing aircraft. In the letter of intent in July 2026, the company said it planned to use the jets for charter and aircraft management services.

THC is also expanding its helicopter fleet. At Farnborough, it placed a firm order for eight additional Airbus H145 helicopters , scheduled for delivery in 2027 and 2028.

Captain Arnaud Martinez, Chief Executive Officer of THC, said the Bombardier agreement marks the company’s entry into business aviation, citing growing demand in Saudi Arabia and the wider…
items.t: Saudi THC firms up 12-jet Bombardier order, with options for 48 more

items.title: BA-owner IAG offers access to 122M travelers through new advertising firm
items.summary:
International Airlines Group (IAG), owner of British Airways and Iberia, is offering businesses and brands access to 122 million travelers a year through its new media and advertising firm.

On November 12, 2026, the company launched IAG Media, aiming to bring together advertising across all IAG airlines for the first time.

As well as the UK’s British Airways and Spain’s Iberia, IAG also owns Aer Lingus, Vueling and LEVEL.

With such an interlinked advertising framework, IAG believes it can use its scale, customer insights and growing onboard connectivity to help brands reach travelers at various points in their journey.

Lukas Wunderlich / Shutterstock 

This will include digital channels, such as in-flight entertainment and the Starlink Wi-Fi login portal, as well as advertising in airport lounges and inflight magazines.

Nacho Tovar, CEO of IAG Media, described travel as “one of the few moments when people are open to discovering new things,” and suggested that the new platform can “put brands right there with them”.

“It brings together the scale of more than 122 million customers with the breadth and diversity of our leading airline brands,” Tovar said. “Each of our airlines serve different customers and markets, giving us access to a highly diverse audience. By combining those insights with on-board connectivity, we can help brands reach customers with advertising that is much more relevant.”

Tovar added: “Our ambition is to build IAG Media into the leading travel media network.”

According to IAG, its strategy is to develop “capital-light, complementary…
items.t: BA-owner IAG offers access to 122M travelers through new advertising firm

items.title: SpiceJet flights from Dubai cancelled over unpaid airport fees: reports
items.summary:
Several SpiceJet flights from Dubai have been cancelled due to unpaid airport fees, according to reports shared by assorted Indian news websites.

On November 13, 2026, the Hindustan Times claimed that four SpiceJet flights from Dubai to Amritsar, Jaipur, Mumbai and Delhi had been cancelled on November 12, 2026, due to the carrier owing AED 14 million ($3.8 million).

According to the publication, Dubai Airports, which manages Dubai International Airport (DXB) and Al Maktoum International Airport (DWC), emailed SpiceJet to advise the airline that it had not received payment since October 13, 2026.

Dubai Airports also advised SpiceJet that check-in services would be suspended due to non-adherence to payment conditions, the report said.

Venkat Mangudi / Creative Commons 

According to Flightradar24 data, a SpiceJet flight scheduled from Dubai International to Delhi on November 13, 2026, at 09:50, local time, was cancelled, as was a flight to Mumbai at 12:20.

Further flights on November 13, 2026, to Amritsar and Jaipur have also been cancelled.

A SpiceJet spokesperson told the Hindustan Times that the airline was working with the relevant authorities to rectify the situation.

“We have adequate bank guarantee cover in place and are working to ensure that the issue is sorted out at the earliest,” the spokesperson said.

SpiceJet financial woes 

In September 2026, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) declared that it was monitoring the carrier to ensure its financial problems do not compromise safety . SpiceJet has been struggling with cash shortages, flight…
items.t: SpiceJet flights from Dubai cancelled over unpaid airport fees: reports

items.title: Japan could slash F-35 fighter purchases amid defense budget clash
items.summary:
Japan’s Ministry of Finance has proposed a five-year defense budget well below the level that some defense officials had expected.  

Citing four people familiar with the discussions, Reuters reported on November 13, 2026 , that the gap could force cuts of up to 50% to some planned aircraft and missile purchases, including Lockheed Martin F-35 fighters. 

According to the report, Finance Ministry officials proposed spending between 50 trillion and 60 trillion yen ($313 billion to $375 billion) on defense over five years beginning from April 2027.  

That would exceed the approximately 43 trillion yen ($269 billion) allocated under Japan’s current Defense Buildup Program for fiscal years 2023 to 2027. However, it would also fall well short of the roughly 80 trillion yen ($500 billion) that some defense officials and ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) lawmakers had anticipated and used in negotiations with contractors. 

Japanese defense contractors warned of potential order cuts 

According to the sources, Japanese officials have warned defense contractors that expected orders could be cut sharply. Japan’s largest defense manufacturers include Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI), Mitsubishi Electric and Kawasaki Heavy Industries. 

One of the sources suggested that drone purchases could be spared. The Japan Ground Self-Defense Force has been evaluating systems in that category, including Helsing’s HX-2 strike drone . Rakuten previously said field trials of the HX-2 would continue through September 2026. 

According to three of the sources, Finance Ministry officials…
items.t: Japan could slash F-35 fighter purchases amid defense budget clash

items.title: A380 startup Global Airlines ordered into compulsory liquidation by UK court
items.summary:
Airbus A380 startup Global Airlines has been ordered into compulsory liquidation by the Insolvency and Companies Court in the United Kingdom (UK).

On November 12, 2026, The Gazette, an official public record, published a formal notice confirming that the court had granted a ‘Winding-Up Order’ on November 4, 2026. This followed a ‘Petition to Wind Up’ that was filed with the UK court in May 2026.

According to the UK government, individuals can apply to the court to close or wind up a company if it cannot pay its debts, also known as compulsory liquidation.

Since the petition was first made, several hearings have been scheduled over the past few months at the Insolvency and Companies Court. It is understood that the most recent court hearing was held in October 2026.

Global Airlines 

Among those that joined the case as supporting creditors were former Global Airlines company directors Tom Stokely and Prashant Uttamchandani. Both individuals were represented by law firm Katten Muchin Rosenman.

In line with a winding-up order, an officer of the court, known as the ‘Official Receiver’ is put in charge of winding-up the company.

By UK government guidelines, when a company receives a winding-up order its bank account will usually be frozen and its assets or property will be sold by the official receiver.

An application can be made to cancel a winding-up order if the company does not feel that it needs to pay its creditors. This must be done within five working days of getting the order.

On the Companies House website, Global Airlines still shows as an active company.…
items.t: A380 startup Global Airlines ordered into compulsory liquidation by UK court

items.title: ‘Build an airport that can adapt.’ Alton Aviation’s Mabel Kwan on APAC financing
items.summary:
Asia Pacific is expected to drive more than half of global aviation growth in the coming decades. Building airports equipped to handle this traffic will cost a great deal. But who is going to pay for it?

This was a question posed at the Passenger Terminal Expo Asia 2026 in Singapore, during a rather aptly titled panel discussion, “Who will finance the future of airports in the Asia Pacific region?”

After the session, AeroTime sat down with panel moderator Mabel Kwan, Managing Director at Alton Aviation Consultancy, which advises governments and investors on airport strategy and public-private partnerships (PPPs), to talk about where the money will come from and why airports built too far ahead of demand can become white elephants.

She also explained why the traffic shift caused by the Middle East conflict is a weaker investment case than it looks.

The US$2.4 trillion question 

Kwan put the scale of the challenge in numbers. Around US$2.4 trillion is set to go into airport infrastructure worldwide, and much of it will be spent in Asia Pacific.

“Asia Pacific is going to be the key region driving aviation growth, contributing to over half of the growth within the aviation industry in the next few decades,” she said. “So we need to think about how to finance and how to support that growth.”

For many countries in the region, airports are about more than capacity. Kwan described them as national strategic assets whose connectivity has a multiplier effect on the wider economy.

That makes the financing question harder, not easier. 

“This infrastructure tends to be…
items.t: ‘Build an airport that can adapt.’ Alton Aviation’s Mabel Kwan on APAC financing

items.title: Avelo opens Dallas-area base with 11 new routes planned
items.summary:
Avelo Airlines opened its fifth US base at McKinney National Airport (DTX) on November 11, 2026, with a flight to Fort Myers, Florida. It was the first scheduled passenger flight to operate from the Dallas-area airport, where Avelo plans to serve 11 nonstop destinations by December 17.

Avelo has based three 184-seat Boeing 737-800s at McKinney, accounting for about a fifth of its 17-aircraft fleet. The airline expects the base to support 150 jobs for pilots, flight attendants, mechanics and airport staff.

McKinney had served general aviation for more than 40 years before Avelo Flight 1848 departed for Fort Myers. The city broke ground on a passenger terminal in Summer 2025, then opened it on the morning of the inaugural flight. The 46,000-square-foot building has four gates and space for two more. According to airport officials, it can handle more than two million passengers a year.

Avelo initially announced five destinations from McKinney in June 2026 and added six more before the first departure. Florida accounts for six of the 11 routes. Fort Myers has four flights a week, while Las Vegas and Orlando are scheduled for six each beginning November 12. Fort Lauderdale and Tampa follow on November 19.

The schedule adds Atlanta, Denver and Sarasota/Bradenton as of December 16. Nashville, New Orleans and West Palm Beach follow a day later, each with flights on Thursdays and Sundays.

Avelo laid out its plans for a North Texas base in January, as part of a broader restructuring. At the time, the carrier announced that it would close bases at Phoenix-Mesa Gateway,…
items.t: Avelo opens Dallas-area base with 11 new routes planned

items.title: Google agrees to privacy safeguards in Spirit Airlines data deal
items.summary:
Google has agreed to keep employee medical files, disciplinary records and safety reports out of its proposed purchase of Spirit Airlines’ internal data. The agreement prompted unions representing former Spirit employees to withdraw their objections to the sale, ahead of a bankruptcy court hearing in New York on November 17, 2026.

Google bid $10 million for the records at an August 14 auction, as Spirit sold off assets after it stopped flying in May . Google intends to use the data to train artificial intelligence models. The material Spirit originally offered included decades of company emails, employee training and travel records, and messages staff exchanged on Microsoft Teams.

The Association of Flight Attendants-CWA challenged the sale four days after the auction. In its filing, the union argued that the proposed terms focused on removing information that could identify a customer, even though much of what Google stood to acquire documented the working lives of Spirit employees. The machinists’ union and Transport Workers Union Local 570 joined the objection.

Spirit’s pilots raised a separate concern about what might happen to information they had shared in confidence. In a court filing, the Air Line Pilots Association cited reports submitted through FAA-approved safety programs. The union suggested that pilots at other airlines could become less willing to report an incident if they believed a future buyer might obtain the report and identify the pilot who filed it.

Under the revised terms, Spirit would hire Tonic AI to strip identifying information from the…
items.t: Google agrees to privacy safeguards in Spirit Airlines data deal

items.title: Four killed in Turkish military S-70 helicopter crash
items.summary:
Four Turkish service members died when a military Sikorsky S-70 helicopter crashed on the outskirts of Malatya in eastern Turkey on November 12, 2026, the country’s Defense Ministry has declared.

The helicopter came down at about 18:45 local time in a neighborhood in Malatya’s Yeşilyurt district, according to local media. Police, firefighters and medical teams responded to the crash. Footage aired by Turkish broadcasters showed flames and smoke rising from the wreckage as emergency vehicles gathered nearby.

The Defense Ministry said it had yet to determine what caused the crash. Its initial statement identified the aircraft as an S-70, but gave no details about the mission or the roles of those aboard.

The Malatya chief public prosecutor’s office has opened an investigation into the crash. A deputy chief prosecutor and two prosecutors have been assigned to the case, Turkey’s Anadolu Agency reported.

Turkey has operated Sikorsky Black Hawk helicopters for decades. Its armed forces already had more than 100 UH-60s in service in 2016, when Sikorsky and Turkish Aerospace Industries launched a program to build a version of the S-70i domestically under license.

The Turkish-built helicopter carries the designation T70. The program calls for 109 helicopters for six military and civilian operators, including Turkey’s land forces, air force and gendarmerie.

Turkish Aerospace delivered the first T70 to the gendarmerie in late 2022. The original order also included 20 helicopters configured for firefighting for Turkey’s forestry service.

The post Four killed in Turkish military…
items.t: Four killed in Turkish military S-70 helicopter crash

items.title: Archer Aviation and Formula 1 partnership could see air taxi flights at races
items.summary:
Archer Aviation and Formula 1 have signed a multi-year partnership that could see air taxi flights at Grand Prix circuits during the motor racing season.

On November 12, 2026, both Archer Aviation and Formula 1 confirmed that the two parties will explore opportunities to introduce electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft services at select events in the calendar year.

The agreement also includes Archer’s presence as an official supporter at events which align with key commercial markets that the company plans to operate in such as the US, Middle East, Asia and Europe.

Archer’s vision for Formula 1 air taxi services includes flying VIPs, stakeholders and fans to and from race circuits using the developer’s eVTOL aircraft ‘Midnight’.

Archer Aviation 

Formula 1 events are typically spread over a long weekend with drivers conducting practice sessions and qualifying rounds, culminating in the championship race on the final day.

According to Archer, the partnership will look at providing dedicated air taxi drop-off and pick-up locations at circuits and offering eVTOL flights as part of Formula 1’s hospitality and ticketing offerings.

“With 830 million fans worldwide, Formula 1 gives us a global audience of prospective passengers who are as obsessed with high-performance vehicles as we are,” Adam Goldstein, founder and CEO of Archer, said. “Motorsport and aerospace share the same engineering DNA, which made this a natural partnership.”

Goldstein added: “We look forward to working with Formula 1 to explore new technologies and how innovation on the ground…
items.t: Archer Aviation and Formula 1 partnership could see air taxi flights at races

items.title: BAE Systems raises cash flow outlook as GCAP, missile orders grow
items.summary:
BAE Systems has raised its free cash flow forecast for 2026 to about £3 billion ($4 billion), up from its previous expectation of more than £2 billion ($2.7 billion), according to a market update published on November 12, 2026. 

Customer advances have helped boost the figure. The revised forecast takes into account payments already received but excludes any large advances that could arrive before the end of the year. Such payments also contributed to the £1.79 billion ($2.4 billion) in free cash flow BAE Systems reported for the first half of 2026. 

The company left its sales and earnings forecasts unchanged from July 2026. It still expects sales to grow by 8% to 10% from £30.7 billion ($40.7 billion) in 2025, underlying earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) by 10% to 12%, and underlying earnings per share (EPS) by 11% to 13%. 

Business remained strong across Electronic Systems, Air, and Platforms & Services, helping offset weaker growth and margins in Maritime. 

GCAP fighter contracts boost BAE Systems orders 

BAE Systems said it had secured £33 billion ($43.8 billion) in orders so far in 2026 and expects further agreements before the end of the year. At the same stage in 2025, it had reported more than £27 billion ($35.8 billion) in orders. 

The company booked about £1.6 billion ($2.1 billion) in orders related to the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP), including its share of the £4.6 billion ($6.1 billion) contract awarded to Edgewing in July 2026. Its share of MBDA orders added approximately £1.5 billion ($2 billion). 

BAE Systems also listed a contract worth…
items.t: BAE Systems raises cash flow outlook as GCAP, missile orders grow

items.title: Korean Air returns to Newark with daily Seoul service from May 2027
items.summary:
Korean Air has announced that it will launch a new daily nonstop service between Seoul-Incheon (ICN) and Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), New Jersey. 

The new service, which was announced on November 12, 2026, will start on May 22, 2027, and will be operated with Boeing 777-300ER aircraft. 

The US-bound flight will depart Seoul at 22.00, local time, and arrive in Newark at 23.00, local time. The return leg will depart Newark at 01.00 and arrive in Seoul at 05:15, local time. 

The Korean carrier will be returning to Newark Liberty International after a 25-year hiatus. Korean Air used to serve the New Jersey gateway, but the route was discontinued in 2001 following the 9/11 attacks and were never reinstated. 

Korean Air does already serve the New York City area directly through a twice-daily service to John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK). According to Cirium SRS Analyzer data , at least one of these two services is operated by Airbus A380 aircraft.  

At the same time, the airline’s recently acquired fully owned subsidiary Asiana Airlines also operates two additional daily frequencies to JFK.  

At Newark, Korean Air will compete with United Airlines and privately-owned Korean carrier Air Premia, which both operate daily services to Seoul using Boeing 787-9 aircraft.

items.t: Korean Air returns to Newark with daily Seoul service from May 2027

items.title: Vertical says new quality certification matches Airbus and Boeing standards
items.summary:
Electric vehicle takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft developer Vertical Aerospace has said a newly awarded quality certification matches the standard used by Airbus and Boeing.

On November 12, 2026, Vertical Aerospace announced the British Standards Institution (BSI) had granted the company AS9100 certification, a globally recognized standard within aerospace.

According to Vertical Aerospace, the certification confirms that its “quality management system across design and production meets the standards used by manufacturers such as Airbus and Boeing”.

The UK firm added that for potential customers the new certification “provides independent assurance in the processes, facilities, suppliers and teams behind Vertical’s future aircraft production and delivery”.

Vertical Aerospace 

Vertical, which is making rigorous, elevated standards a key part of its business framework, believes it is the first eVTOL developer to achieve the AS9100 certification.

“We are leading the way in electric aviation by holding ourselves to the highest standards in aerospace,” Stuart Simpson, CEO of Vertical Aerospace, said. “Achieving AS9100 means our quality management system is certified against the same standard used by established manufacturers such as Airbus and Boeing. It is what our customers expect. That is the discipline we are bringing to Valo, and to building a company customers can depend on.”

Developed by the International Aerospace Quality Group (IAQG), AS9100 builds on ISO 9001 with requirements specific to aviation, space and defense.

Vertical said it achieved certification…
items.t: Vertical says new quality certification matches Airbus and Boeing standards

items.title: Czechia eyes supplying Ukraine with 16 L-39 Skyfox light combat jets
items.summary:
Czechia could supply Ukraine with up to 16 Aero Vodochody L-39 Skyfox jets, First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Industry and Trade Karel Havlíček told reporters in Kyiv on November 11, 2026. 

Havlíček, who was leading a Czech business mission to Ukraine, said four aircraft had previously been confirmed and that he had discussed the supply of another 12 with Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi. 

The talks had produced a “preliminary confirmation” that the additional aircraft could be supplied, according to the Czech News Agency (ČTK) . 

Skyfox emerges after Czechia rejects L-159 transfer 

The discussions follow Ukraine’s earlier attempt to acquire four L-159 ALCA light combat aircraft from the Czech Air Force to counter Russian drones. 

President Petr Pavel raised the prospect of a transfer during a visit to Kyiv on January 16, 2026. Three days later, Prime Minister Andrej Babiš ruled out selling or donating the jets , saying the armed forces needed them. 

Aero Vodochody has said it can no longer build new L-159s because some components are unavailable. In January 2026, the manufacturer offered the Skyfox as an alternative.

items.t: Czechia eyes supplying Ukraine with 16 L-39 Skyfox light combat jets

items.title: Boeing slide in 737 MAX deliveries hampers recent progress
items.summary:
Boeing saw a slide in its 737 MAX deliveries in October 2026, hampering recent progress made by the US planemaker following the summer months.

On November 11, 2026, Boeing confirmed it delivered 49 aircraft in October 2026, a decrease from 57 deliveries in September 2026.

In August 2026, Boeing delivered 51 aircraft and in July 2026, the company delivered 53. The company’s strongest month this year was in June when 64 planes reached customers.

There was noticeable dip in MAX deliveries over October 2026, with only 32 aircraft making it out of the factory. In September 2026, the figure was 43 and in August 2026, 41.

Riyadh Air 

In September 2026, Boeing President and CEO Kelly Ortberg said that while 737 production is “now driving at 47 a month” it is not yet “stable” and it had taken a “little bit longer” than he had anticipated to increase from 42 to 47 aircraft a month.

Ortberg also pointed to constraints in 737 wing production and that Boeing had “not seen the flow improvements that we expected in the time frame”.

Dreamliner deliveries increased in October 2026, with 11 787s handed over to customers. However, the raised figure suggests Boeing was clearing a backlog rather than an acceleration in production.

Among the airlines that received new aircraft were flydubai, Air New Zealand, Akasa Air and United Airlines.

With two months of the year remaining, Boeing has so far delivered 524 aircraft in 2026. At the same stage in 2025, Boeing had delivered 493 planes and by the end of the year the total stood at 600.

items.t: Boeing slide in 737 MAX deliveries hampers recent progress

items.title: US military to test autonomous Cessna Caravan for casualty evacuation in Morocco
items.summary:
Boston-based Merlin has received a $500,000 contract from US Africa Command (AFRICOM) to demonstrate an autonomous casualty evacuation (CASEVAC) mission using a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan in Morocco, the company announced on November 11, 2026 .

The award covers the initial phase of AFRICOM’s Autonomous CASEVAC Industry Technology Challenge, with the demonstration planned for early US government fiscal year 2027, which began on October 1, 2026.

The mission will run from tasking and flight planning through autonomous departure and flight to an austere casualty collection site. After simulated patient loading, the aircraft will autonomously complete the return flight and landing.

Merlin’s autonomous Cessna Caravan to conduct casualty evacuation 

Merlin said Merlin Pilot is designed to manage flight planning, navigation, contingency response and mission completion without relying on a remote ground station or flight crew.

The software plans a route based on the operator’s tasking, replans around hazards, communicates with air traffic control using natural language processing, and continues along its authorized flight plan if communications are lost, according to the company.

Merlin has not said whether a safety pilot will be aboard for the demonstration. A safety pilot monitored the Caravan’s autonomous landing at EAA AirVenture Oshkosh on July 17, 2026, according to the company.

The Caravan’s large cargo door and flat cabin floor allow stretchers to be loaded at ground level without rotor downwash or winching equipment. The aircraft will carry an air ambulance medical…
items.t: US military to test autonomous Cessna Caravan for casualty evacuation in Morocco

items.title: Emirates strikes deal to take ownership of six Airbus A380 aircraft
items.summary:
Emirates will take ownership of six Airbus A380-800 aircraft currently operated as part of its fleet under a lease agreement with Qatar’s Lesha Bank.

On November 10, 2026, Lesha Bank confirmed it had reached an agreement to sell six Airbus A380s to Emirates , two of which have already been completed.

Sale of the remaining four A380s are due to be concluded in stages through April 2028, as their respective leases conclude.

“We are pleased to have concluded this sale with Emirates, a long-standing and valued partner.” Jonathan Skirrow, Co-CEO of Lesha Aviation Services, said. “Completing the sale of the two aircraft marks an important milestone, and the phased transfer of the remaining four underscores both the strength of our relationship with the airline and our continued focus on delivering well-structured, value-accretive transactions for our investors.”

Lesha Bank added that the transaction reflects its “growing track record in aviation” and demonstrates the company’s “ability to structure and deliver seamless aircraft transitions that generate strong outcomes for clients and investors alike”.

Emirates A380s leased through Amedeo 

The six A380s were leased to Emirates through Amedeo Air Four Plus which was acquired by Lesha Bank in June 2026.

It is understood that the aircraft include A6-EEY, A6-EOB, A6-EOM, A6-EOQ, A6-EOV and A6-EOX. All are aged between 10 and 12 years old.

items.t: Emirates strikes deal to take ownership of six Airbus A380 aircraft

items.title: United Airlines to block third-party AI agents from accessing digital platforms
items.summary:
In an industry first, United Airlines announced on November 11, 2026, that it is restricting unauthorized third-party artificial intelligence (AI) agents from accessing its digital booking platform. 

The airline said that AI agents pose an unacceptable risk because they could expose sensitive passenger information and take actions which could result in unintended purchases or unwanted changes to customer accounts, including the airline’s MileagePlus loyalty program. 

In a statement United Airlines went even further, expressing concern about the potential violation of Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and Department of Transportation (DOT) security regulations. According to the airline, the use of AI agents to manage passenger bookings may be circumventing rules which require human acknowledgement for some actions, such as stating that bags do not contain any banned or dangerous materials. 

The ban on third- party AI agents also extends to their use through indirect channels such as online travel agents (OTAs) and aggregators. United Airlines said it will be updating its conditions of carriage to reflect this decision. 

The airline also pointed out that the measure is in line with those taken by companies in other industries, such as banking and retail, which also deal with highly sensitive and confidential customer data. 

The use of AI in travel distribution and, by extension, its implications for the industry’s current structure and business model, has been a matter of growing debate within the industry. This has been reflected in the agenda of major industry…
items.t: United Airlines to block third-party AI agents from accessing digital platforms

items.title: Zelenskyy says Starshield speed cap returns, hindering Russian drone interceptions
items.summary:
Starshield, the military-grade version of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite service, is once again losing connectivity on equipment moving faster than 161 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour) in Ukraine, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on November 12, 2026. The restrictions have returned less than three weeks after Kyiv announced that a similar cap had been lifted.

In a post on X, Zelenskyy said Ukrainian units had reported “significant disruptions” to Starshield for several days across the front line and Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine. He cited briefings from Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara and Mykhailo Drapatyi, Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.

According to Zelenskyy, the military investigated the disruptions and concluded they were “not random errors but systematic speed restrictions.” He did not say when the restrictions began or who imposed them, adding that Kyiv was “trying to establish all the circumstances with the American side.”

Specifically, systematic speed restrictions are being imposed on Starshield, limiting it to 161 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour). The Ukrainian military have already investigated the circumstances, and these are not random errors but…
items.t: Zelenskyy says Starshield speed cap returns, hindering Russian drone interceptions

items.title: FAA clears Skyways to test offshore drone deliveries for Shell
items.summary:
The FAA has authorized Skyways, an Austin, Texas-based cargo drone manufacturer and operator, to fly from Gibson, Louisiana, to a Shell platform in the Gulf of Mexico for a pipeline inspection and simulated equipment delivery.

On the planned demonstration flight, the aircraft will inspect a pipeline right-of-way en route to the platform and simulate a delivery of equipment when it arrives.

The FAA announced the waiver allowing the flight on November 9, 2026, describing it as the first US authorization for a drone to fly from the coast out over the Gulf beyond its operator’s visual line of sight.

Skyways will launch its V2 aircraft from Shell Pipeline Company’s facility on the Gulf Coast. The V2 uses electric motors for vertical takeoff and landing, then switches to a heavy-fuel engine for cruise. A satellite link provides command and control offshore.

The FAA granted the waiver under Section 927 of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024. That provision gives the agency a way to authorize specific drone operations that fall outside existing rules.

Shell Pipeline Company already uses drones offshore and has worked with Skyways on pipeline inspections in the Gulf.

The demonstration combines that inspection work with a test of the aircraft’s cargo role.

Skyways said it hopes to use the V2 for more frequent inspections and eventually carry cargo to offshore installations for a fee.

The post FAA clears Skyways to test offshore drone deliveries for Shell appeared first on AeroTime .
items.t: FAA clears Skyways to test offshore drone deliveries for Shell

items.title: FAA expands AI traffic planning tool to all 22 US en route centers
items.summary:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said it is expanding the use of its AI-assisted traffic planning tool to airspace managed by all 22 US air route traffic control centers, even after more than two dozen lawmakers called for a pause in its Washington-area rollout.

In announcing the expansion on November 10, 2026, the FAA said the tool had helped reroute 180 flights in the Washington area. The agency reported average savings of 10 minutes and nearly 80 gallons of fuel per rerouted flight.

The system, called Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories (SMART), draws on 200 data streams, including weather, flight paths, traffic volumes and controller staffing. It helps air traffic planners anticipate where demand could exceed capacity and identify opportunities to reroute flights before congestion builds.

FAA specialists at the SMART center in Washington review the data and send scheduling recommendations to the agency’s Air Traffic Control System Command Center in Warrenton, Virginia. The command center passes those recommendations to the facilities responsible for the affected airspace. Local managers then decide whether to act on them.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford unveiled SMART on September 21, 2026 , when the agency began limited operations involving flights at Reagan National (DCA), Washington Dulles (IAD) and Baltimore/Washington International (BWI) airports.

In October, the lawmakers asked the FAA to explain how it had tested the system for safety and trained staff to use it. The agency’s November 10…
items.t: FAA expands AI traffic planning tool to all 22 US en route centers

items.title: easyJet shareholders approve Apollo’s £5.7 billion takeover bid
items.summary:
easyJet shareholders approved Apollo’s proposed £5.7 billion ($7.6 billion) takeover on November 11, 2026. The UK low-cost carrier expects the deal to close by the end of March 2027, subject to court and regulatory approvals. Completion would end easyJet’s London Stock Exchange listing after more than 25 years.

At a court-convened shareholder meeting, 97.07% of votes cast favored the takeover. At a separate general meeting, 96.67% of votes cast backed a resolution to implement the deal and amend easyJet’s articles of association.

Apollo’s cash offer values each easyJet share at £7.15. Shareholders can also elect to exchange their entire holding for unlisted shares in the new parent company.

Founder Sir Stelios Haji-Ioannou and his family, who together held about 15.3% of easyJet when the deal was announced, chose that option.

The vote followed a summer bidding contest between two US investment firms. In June, easyJet’s board rejected a £6.25-per-share offer from private equity firm Castlelake. Apollo and easyJet reached an agreement in principle at £7.15 per share on July 10. After Castlelake withdrew, easyJet’s board recommended Apollo’s offer on August 6.

At the general meeting, easyJet suspended voting rights on 233.9 million shares held by non-EU investors to comply with European ownership and control rules. EU investors held 35.07% of easyJet’s shares at the time of the meeting, the airline said.

Under the proposed ownership structure, Apollo’s funds would hold no more than 49.9% of the new parent company. Apollo has also committed to keeping easyJet’s…
items.t: easyJet shareholders approve Apollo’s £5.7 billion takeover bid
